rankle.sentence: a splinter rankles in the flesh

raspy.enDef: (of sound) Rough, raw, especially used to describe vocal quality.
raspy.sentence: His incessant coughing made his voice sound raspy.

raucous.sentence: At night, raucous sounds come from the swamp.

rave.enDef: An enthusiastic review (such as of a play).

razor.enDef: A keen-edged knife of peculiar shape, used in shaving the hair from the face or other parts of the body.

rebuff.sentence: He was surprised by her quick rebuff to his proposal.

recant.enDef: To withdraw or repudiate a statement or opinion formerly expressed, especially formally and publicly.
recant.sentence: Convince me that I am wrong, and I will recant.

reclaim.enDef: The calling back of a hawk.

recline.enDef: A mechanism for lowering the back of a seat to support a less upright position; Also, the action of lowering the back using such a mechanism.
recline.sentence: She reclined her arms on the table and sighed.

reed.enDef: Any of various types of tall stiff perennial grass-like plants growing together in groups near water.

refectory.enDef: A dining-hall, especially in an institution such as a college or monastery.

refraction.enDef: The turning or bending of any wave, such as a light or sound wave, when it passes from one medium into another of different optical density.

relegate.enDef: Exile, banish, remove, or send away.

relent.sentence: He had planned to ground his son for a month, but relented and decided to give him a stern lecture instead.

remorse.enDef: A feeling of regret or sadness for doing wrong or sinning.

rendition.enDef: The surrender (of a city, fortress etc.).

repatriate.enDef: A person who has returned to the country of origin or whose citizenship has been restored.

repent.enDef: To feel pain, sorrow, or regret for what one has done or omitted to do; the cause for repenting may be indicated with "of".
repent.sentence: If you are a true Muslim, you should repent to Allah.

reprieve.enDef: The cancellation or postponement of a punishment.

repugnant.enDef: Offensive or repulsive; arousing disgust or aversion.

requisite.sentence: Please submit the requisite papers before the end of the financial year.

rescind.enDef: To repeal, annul, or declare void; to take (something such as a rule or contract) out of effect.
rescind.sentence: The agency will rescind the policy because many people are dissatisfied with it.

residual.enDef: A remainder left over at the end of some process.

resigned.enDef: To sign again; to provide one's signature again.
resigned.sentence: He resigned the crown to follow his heart.

resilient.enDef: (of objects or substances) Returning quickly to original shape after force is applied; elastic.

resonant.sentence: From across the valley came the resonant sound of a distant church bell.

respite.enDef: A brief interval of rest or relief.

restitution.enDef: A process of compensation for losses.
restitution.sentence: the restitution of an elastic body

restored.enDef: To reestablish, or bring back into existence.
restored.sentence: He restored my lost faith in him by doing a good deed.

retainer.enDef: Any thing or person that retains.
retainer.sentence: This lawyer charges a retainer for his work.

reticent.enDef: Keeping one's thoughts and opinions to oneself; reserved or restrained.

revealing.enDef: To uncover; to show and display that which was hidden.

reverie.enDef: A state of dreaming while awake; a loose or irregular train of thought; musing or meditation; daydream.

rift.sentence: My marriage is in trouble: the fight created a rift between us and we can't reconnect.

rinse.sentence: I'll just give this knife a quick rinse.

ripple.enDef: A moving disturbance, or undulation, in the surface of a fluid.
ripple.sentence: I dropped a small stone into the pond and watched the ripples spread.

robe.enDef: A long loose outer garment, often signifying honorary stature.

rookie.enDef: An inexperienced recruit, especially in the police or armed forces.
rookie.sentence: The game was going well until I made that rookie mistake.

roster.enDef: A list of individuals or groups, usually for an organization of some kind such as military officers and enlisted personnel enrolled in a particular unit; a muster roll; a sports team, with the names of players who are eligible to be placed in the lineup for a particular game; or a list of students officially enrolled in a school or class.
roster.sentence: The secretary has produced a new cleaning roster for the Church over the remainder of the year.

roundabout.enDef: (Australia and sometimes United States) A road junction at which traffic streams circularly around a central island.

rubble.enDef: The broken remains of an object, usually rock or masonry.

ruse.enDef: A turning or doubling back, especially of animals to get out of the way of hunting dogs.

rustle.enDef: A soft crackling sound similar to the movement of dry leaves.

sabotage.enDef: A deliberate action aimed at weakening an enemy through subversion, obstruction, disruption, and/or destruction.
sabotage.sentence: The railway line had been sabotaged by enemy commandos.

sagacious.enDef: Having or showing keen discernment, sound judgment, and farsightedness; mentally shrewd.

sage.enDef: A wise person or spiritual teacher; someone of gravity and wisdom, especially, a teacher venerable for years, and of sound judgment and prudence; a grave or stoic philosopher.

saliva.enDef: A clear, slightly alkaline liquid secreted into the mouth by the salivary glands and mucous glands, consisting of water, mucin, protein, and enzymes. It moistens the mouth, lubricates ingested food, and begins the breakdown of starches.

salubrious.enDef: Promoting health or well-being; wholesome, especially as related to air.

sane.enDef: Being in a healthy condition; not deranged; thinking rationally.

sap.enDef: The juice of plants of any kind, especially the ascending and descending juices or circulating fluid essential to nutrition.

saturated.enDef: To cause to become completely impregnated, or soaked (especially with a liquid).
saturated.sentence: After walking home in the driving rain, his clothes were saturated.

savant.enDef: A person of learning, especially one who is versed in literature or science.

schism.enDef: A split or separation within a group or organization, typically caused by discord.
schism.sentence: The schism between Sunnis and Shias happened quite early in Islamic history.

screwdriver.enDef: A hand or machine tool which engages with the head of a screw and allows torque to be applied to turn the screw, thus driving it in or loosening it.

scroll.enDef: A roll of paper or parchment; a writing formed into a roll.
scroll.sentence: I ordered a glass of lemonade and a coffee scroll.

sculptor.enDef: A person who sculpts; an artist who produces sculpture.

sequester.sentence: The jury was sequestered from the press by the judge's order.

serenade.enDef: A love song that is sung directly to one's love interest, especially one performed below the window of a loved one in the evening.
serenade.sentence: “Eine kleine Nachtmusik” is a well-known serenade written by Mozart.

serendipity.enDef: A combination of events which have come together by chance to make a surprisingly good or wonderful outcome.

shard.enDef: A piece of broken glass or pottery, especially one found in an archaeological dig.

shawl.enDef: A square or rectangular piece of cloth worn as a covering for the head, neck, and shoulders, typically by women.
shawl.sentence: She wears her shawl when it's cold outside.

sheath.enDef: A holster for a sword; a scabbard.

sheriff.enDef: (except Scotland) (High Sheriff) An official of a shire or county office, responsible for carrying out court orders, law enforcement and other duties.

sibling.enDef: A person who shares a parent; one's brother or sister who one shares a parent with.
sibling.sentence: None of my siblings are married yet.

sill.enDef: (also window sill) A horizontal slat which forms the base of a window.

siren.enDef: One of a group of nymphs who lured mariners to their death on the rocks.

skew.enDef: Something that has an oblique or slanted position.
skew.sentence: A disproportionate number of female subjects in the study group skewed the results.

slate.enDef: A fine-grained homogeneous sedimentary rock composed of clay or volcanic ash which has been metamorphosed so that it cleaves easily into thin layers.
slate.sentence: Put it on my slate – I’ll pay you next week.

slay.sentence: Our foes must all be slain.

smug.sentence: Kate looked extremely smug this morning.

snub.sentence: I hope the people we couldn't invite don't see it as a snub.

snug.enDef: A small, comfortable back room in a pub.
snug.sentence: I felt snug tucked up in my snug bed.

somber.enDef: To make sombre or dark; to make shady.

sonata.enDef: A musical composition for one or a few instruments, one of which is frequently a piano, in three or four movements that vary in key and tempo.

spat.enDef: To evacuate (saliva or another substance) from the mouth, etc.
spat.sentence: a hot pan spitting droplets of fat

spike.enDef: In a violin-family instrument, the carved wooden plug which sits in the bottom block of the instrument.
spike.sentence: The trap was lined with spikes.

splint.enDef: An inferior kind of cannel coal from Scottish collieries, having a slaty structure.

spoke.enDef: A support structure that connects the axle or the hub of a wheel to the rim.

sprain.enDef: The act or result of spraining; lameness caused by spraining
sprain.sentence: a bad sprain of the wrist

sprint.enDef: A short race at top speed.

spruce.enDef: Any of various large coniferous evergreen trees or shrubs from the genus Picea, found in northern temperate and boreal regions; originally and more fully spruce fir.

spurious.sentence: His argument was spurious and had no validity.

squint.enDef: An expression in which the eyes are partly closed.
squint.sentence: He looks handsome although he's got a slight squint.

stranded.sentence: Jones pops up; that's going to strand a pair.

stupor.enDef: A state of reduced consciousness or sensibility.

subsidiary.enDef: A company owned by a parent company or a holding company, also called daughter company or sister company.

sundry.enDef: (usually in the plural) A minor miscellaneous item.

superfluous.enDef: In excess of what is required or sufficient.
superfluous.sentence: With a full rain suit, carrying an umbrella may be superfluous.

supernova.enDef: The explosion of a star, which increases its brightness to typically a billion times that of our sun, though attenuated by the great distance from our sun. Some leave only debris (Type I); others fade to invisibility as neutron stars (Type II).

supine.enDef: (grammar) In Latin and other languages: a type of verbal noun used in the ablative and accusative cases, which shares the same stem as the passive participle.

surly.sentence: The surly weather put us all in a bad mood.

susceptibility.enDef: The condition of being susceptible; vulnerability

syllabus.enDef: A summary of topics which will be covered during an academic course, or a text or lecture.

taciturn.enDef: Silent; temperamentally untalkative; disinclined to speak.
taciturn.sentence: The two sisters could hardly have been more different, one so boisterous and expressive, the other so taciturn and calm.

taking.enDef: To get into one's hands, possession or control, with or without force.
taking.sentence: I'll take that plate off the table.

tambourine.enDef: A percussion instrument consisting of a small, usually wooden, hoop closed on one side with a drum frame and featuring jingling metal disks on the tread; it is most often held in the hand and shaken rhythmically; by extension, any frame drum.

tantamount.enDef: Something which has the same value or amount (as something else). (attributive use passing into adjective, below)
tantamount.sentence: In this view, disagreement and treason are tantamount.

taut.enDef: To make taut; to tauten, to tighten.

tenet.enDef: An opinion, belief, or principle that is held as absolute truth by someone or especially an organization.

terse.enDef: (by extension) Of speech or style: brief, concise, to the point.

tether.enDef: A rope, cable etc. that holds something in place whilst allowing some movement

tiff.enDef: A small argument; a petty quarrel.

toady.enDef: A sycophant who flatters others to gain personal advantage or an obsequious lackey or minion

tombstone.enDef: A headstone marking a person's grave.

toxin.enDef: A toxic or poisonous substance produced by the biological processes of biological organisms.

trajectory.enDef: The path an object takes as it moves.

tramp.enDef: (sometimes derogatory) A homeless person; a vagabond.
tramp.sentence: "Claudia is such a tramp; making out with all those men when she has a boyfriend."

trespass.enDef: An intentional interference with another's property or person.

tribunal.enDef: An assembly including one or more judges to conduct judicial business; a court of law.

trio.enDef: A group of three people or things.

troll.enDef: A supernatural being of varying size, now especially a grotesque humanoid creature living in caves or hills or under bridges.

truce.enDef: A period of time in which no fighting takes place due to an agreement between the opposed parties

tussle.sentence: The two sets of fans were tussling before the game.

typhoon.enDef: A weather phenomenon in the northwestern Pacific that is precisely equivalent to a hurricane, which results in wind speeds of 64 knots (118 km/h) or above. Equivalent to a cyclone in the Indian Ocean and Indonesia/Australia.

ubiquitous.sentence: To Hindus, Jews, Christians, and Muslims, God is ubiquitous.

ulcer.enDef: An open sore of the skin, eyes or mucous membrane, often caused by an initial abrasion and generally maintained by an inflammation and/or an infection.

ulterior.enDef: Situated beyond, or on the farther side.

undercut.enDef: A cut made in the lower part of something; the material so removed.

unicorn.enDef: A mythical beast resembling a horse or deer with a single, straight, spiraled horn projecting from its forehead.

usurp.enDef: To seize power from another, usually by illegitimate means.

utensil.enDef: An instrument or device for domestic use, especially in the kitchen.
utensil.sentence: We have convenient storage for all the kitchen utensils.

vacillate.enDef: To sway unsteadily from one side to the other; oscillate.

vanilla.enDef: Any tropical, climbing orchid of the genus Vanilla (especially Vanilla planifolia), bearing podlike fruit yielding an extract used in flavoring food or in perfumes.
vanilla.sentence: You can tell that the secret ingredient missing from New CokeTM was vanilla, because certain South American economies collapsed when it was introduced, and miraculously revived when the old formula was used again.

variance.enDef: The act of varying or the state of being variable.
variance.sentence: Depending on the variance of the type constructor, the subtyping relation of the simple types may be either preserved, reversed, or ignored for the respective complex types.

veneer.enDef: A thin decorative covering of fine material (usually wood) applied to coarser wood or other material.
veneer.sentence: to veneer a piece of furniture with mahogany

vengeance.enDef: Revenge taken for an insult, injury, or other wrong.

veracity.enDef: (of a person) The quality of speaking or stating the truth; truthfulness.

verbose.enDef: Abounding in words, containing more words than necessary; long-winded.

vernacular.enDef: The language of a people or a national language.
vernacular.sentence: A vernacular of the United States is English.

viaduct.enDef: A bridge with several spans that carries road or rail traffic over a valley or other obstacles.

vindictive.enDef: Having a tendency to seek revenge when wronged, vengeful.

violet.enDef: A monocotyledonous plant (Allium cepa), allied to garlic, used as vegetable and spice.

volition.sentence: Out of all the factors that can influence a person’s decision, none can match the power of his or her own volition.

voluble.enDef: (of a person or a manner of speaking) Fluent or having a ready flow of speech; garrulous or loquacious; tonguey.

weld.enDef: A herb (Reseda luteola) related to mignonette, growing in Europe, and to some extent in America, used to make a yellow dye.

wheeze.enDef: A piping or whistling sound caused by difficult respiration.
wheeze.sentence: The new comedy is a wheeze.

whimper.sentence: The lonely puppy began to whimper as soon as we left the room.

wiggle.enDef: A rapid movement in alternating opposite directions, not necessarily regular.
wiggle.sentence: She walked with a sexy wiggle.

winding.enDef: To blow air through a wind instrument or horn to make a sound.
winding.sentence: The boxer was winded during round two.

woe.enDef: Great sadness or distress; a misfortune causing such sadness.

woo.enDef: To endeavor to gain someone's support.

wraith.enDef: A ghost or specter, especially a person's likeness seen just after their death.

wrought.enDef: To do a specific task by employing physical or mental powers.

xenophobia.enDef: A fear of strangers or foreigners.

yank.enDef: A sudden, vigorous pull (sometimes defined as mass times jerk, or rate of change of force).
yank.sentence: They yanked the product as soon as they learned it was unsafe.

zenith.enDef: The point in the sky vertically above a given position or observer; the point in the celestial sphere opposite the nadir.
zenith.sentence: Winning the continental championship was the zenith of my career.
